items.title: Artificial Intelligence Scribes and Same-Day Note Closure by Patient Language Preference and Interpreter Modality
items.excerpt: Brigham and Women's cross-sectional study of 209,009 primary-care encounters (286 clinicians, 14 clinics): AI scribes raised same-day note closure most for non-English-language-preference visits with a language-concordant clinician (+10.2 points adjusted vs +1.7 for English); interpreter-mediated visits inconclusive. Date per Crossref created.

items.title: Deep-learning model predicts mortality from CTA scans
items.excerpt: Cedars-Sinai-led multicenter study (1,674 TAVR-planning patients, 9 sites, JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging) shows a deep-learning model quantifies aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue on CTA in 1.35 min vs 7.2 min for experts; highest fibrotic volume carried 2x mortality risk.

items.title: FDA clears AI-powered intravascular ultrasound imaging platform
items.excerpt: FDA cleared Evident Vascular's Guidance System and peripheral IVUS catheters, which integrate 'purpose-built AI' and NVIDIA-accelerated real-time processing for peripheral vascular procedures; the company plans further AI capabilities.

items.title: 루닛, 의료 특화 AI 파운데이션 모델 '러닝유닛 2.0' 전격 공개
items.excerpt: Lunit completed the MSIT medical foundation-model project and open-sourced LearningUnit 2.0 (30B params, 5B active, runs on-premise) on Hugging Face; validated at 9 Korean hospitals — 86.2% of multidisciplinary tumor-board plans judged clinically valid, 98% within-one-level agreement on ER KTAS triage and ADR causality.

items.title: 루닛, 미국면역항암학회서 랩콥·셀카르타와 AI 활용 연구성과 공개
items.excerpt: At SITC 2026 Lunit presents Lunit SCOPE IO studies with Labcorp and Cellcarta: H&E-only AI HRD score in 339 ovarian cancer patients correlated with genomic instability score, informing PARP-inhibitor selection.

items.title: 동탄시티병원, AI로 재택환자 위험 조기 발견…병원·지역사회 잇는 통합돌봄 구축
items.excerpt: 180-bed Dongtan City Hospital, which runs AI for imaging, surgery/rehab and ward monitoring plus a command center, outlined an AI home-care model that flags health changes in homebound patients and routes them to home visits or admission.

items.title: 병원 문턱 넘은 병리 AI…수가와 디지털 전환 비용은 숙제
items.excerpt: Pathology AI in Korean hospitals is shifting from read-assist to treatment-response prediction (e.g., AZ/Daiichi TROP2 biomarker phase 3), but sustained use hinges on reimbursement and digital-conversion costs; demonstrations must feed into benefit evaluation.

items.title: Comparative Cost of Care Recommended by LLMs vs. Treating Physicians
items.excerpt: NEJM AI study: 24 AI systems given 200 real outpatient/ED notes recommended care costing $314 per visit vs $97 for physicians — extra tests, referrals and nearly twice as many new drugs; medical-specific models were no more restrained.

items.title: From pixels to plain English: Introducing SpatialWhisperer
items.excerpt: Stanford Cancer Institute's SpatialWhisperer AI predicts cell types (T cells, tumor cells) from routine H&E pathology slides, replacing costly molecular tests for tumor-ecosystem analysis.

items.title: Patients want a human in the loop for AI healthcare tools
items.excerpt: Survey of 3,488 U.S. adults: patients accept AI for admin tasks like jargon translation and scheduling when a human reviews output, but not for diagnosis or claims adjudication.

items.title: How should the FDA regulate generative AI in medtech? Here are 5 takes
items.excerpt: Patients, providers and medtech firms filed hundreds of comments on FDA's approach to generative AI in medical devices; five positions summarized.

items.title: 7 Potential Problems with Medicare's AI Prior Authorization Experiment
items.excerpt: CMS documents obtained by EFF via FOIA lawsuit detail early problems in the WISeR model, where six tech companies use AI to review Medicare prior authorization requests in six states.

items.title: A gait foundation model for prediction of multisystem health phenotypes from 3D skeletal motion
items.excerpt: Foundation model trained on 3D skeletal motion from 3,328 adults predicts cardiometabolic, mental-health and frailty diagnoses and clinical characteristics from gait.

items.title: AI-driven multi-horizon risk stratification for heart failure hospitalization in UA with HFpEF: a Chinese multi-center cohort study
items.excerpt: Multicenter Chinese cohort: AI model stratifies short- and long-horizon heart-failure hospitalization risk in HFpEF patients with unstable angina.

items.title: RETBind: a patient-level multimodal foundation model for unified cross-modal retinal representation learning
items.excerpt: Patient-level multimodal retinal foundation model binding fundus, OCT and other modalities for ophthalmic diagnostic support.

items.title: Stroke recovery tracked with wearable device
items.excerpt: NIH-funded UMass team used machine learning on wrist accelerometer data from 61 stroke patients to build a digital arm performance scale (DAPS) that tracked arm recovery as well as clinical tests (Science Translational Medicine).

items.title: Parent Comfort With Artificial Intelligence-Led Behavioral Therapy for Their Child
items.excerpt: Boston Children's survey of 572 US parents: 76% not comfortable with AI-led behavioral therapy for their child; comfort strongly tied to parents' own comfort with AI therapy (aOR 20.9).
